MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 13, 2016

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Ury at 5:00 p.m., on September 13, 2016, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 8, 2016, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Public Employee Performance Evaluation: Title: Special/General Counsel: Mission
  Viejo Housing Authority and Successor Agency.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
City Council Minutes  1  September 13, 2016
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Manager Wilberg announced that there was no reportable action from Closed Session.

INVOCATION: Imam Saymeh, Orange County Islamic Foundation

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Ury presented certificates of commendation to "Marine of the Quarter" Lance
  Corporal Eric P. Grill and "Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter" Sergeant Eric
  Gonzales.

P2.  Recognize Solar Power Pools, Lululemon Athletica, and St. Kilian Catholic Church
  as "Certified Green Businesses"

  Mayor Ury presented certificates to the owners or representatives of Solar Power Pools,
  Lululemon Athletica, and St. Kilian Church.

P3.  Presentation by Historian Bob Hayes on Constitution Day

  The City Council received the presentation from Bob Hayes.

P4.  True North Survey Presentation

  The City Council received the presentation from Dr. Tim McLarney, True North Research,
  Inc.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Joseph Lenihan and Renee Daniels, M.V.: on behalf of the American Cancer Society (ACS,) they
gave the City of Mission Viejo a "Presenting Sponsor Award" for the City's participation in the
Relay For Life for the past twenty years. Mr. Lenihan noted that with the City's partnership, the
ACS has raised over $2.5 million including $158,000 in proceeds from this year's Relay.

Travis Williams, M.V.: introduced himself and his new business, a Farmers Insurance agency in
Mission Viejo. He stated that his goal is to help families and businesses protect the assets they
have gathered and to plan for the future.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2 and 8 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.
City Council Minutes  2  September 13, 2016
 Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

3.  Check Register Dated August 12, 2016 in the Amount of $1,926,879.17

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated August 19, 2016 in the Amount of $1,254,786.97

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register Dated August 26, 2016 in the Amount of $1,993,740.65

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Request by the Cultural Arts Committee for a one-time exemption to the "No
  Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" Regulation at the Mission Viejo Library. Event -
  Photography Exhibit Reception and Concert on Friday, September 23, 2016 from 6
  to 10 pm.

  Approved the request of the Cultural Arts Committee for a one-time exemption to the "No
  Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" Regulation for the Photography Exhibit Reception and
  Concert at the Mission Viejo Library.

7.  Destruction of Records – Citywide Annual Records Purge

  Adopt Resolution 16-44 Authorizing and Directing the City Clerk to Destroy Certain City
  Records and Documents Pursuant to the Government Code of the State of California.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

City Council Minutes  3  September 13, 2016
   Council Member Schlicht asked that the Minutes be amended on page 6, to reflect her
  comments about playground equipment for "pre-teens" and "middle school-aged" kids, not
  teens.
  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve the
  Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of August 23, 2016, as amended.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

8.  Mission Viejo Animal Services Administration Building Expansion

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.
  He said that during the course of the project design, City staff determined that it would be
  logical and needed to address some lingering maintenance issues, in the amount of
  $88,677.00 to replace the existing portion of the administration building “built up roof”
  along with the new portion of the built up roof, the existing HVAC components on the roof
  a stand-alone air conditioning unit to keep the IT space cool.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern that the project is over-budget and stated that
  this is basically a change order on the Consent Calendar.

  Mr. Rattay responded that the additional items do not have to be done but staff is
  recommending it while the building is under construction.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to (1)
  award a contract to New Dynasty Construction Co. (A16-33) in an amount not to exceed
  $686,427.00 and issue a purchase order; and (2) adopt Resolution 16-45 Amending the
  CIP 17308 Mission Viejo Animal Services Administration Building Expansion Budget in
  Fund 560.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

9.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

City Council Minutes  4  September 13, 2016
 10.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

11.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

12.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Mayor Ury presented the report.

13.  Update on CUSD Bond Measure Issue

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum mentioned the Capistrano Unified School District Board of
  Directors' threat of a lawsuit and asked if the City has been served. City Attorney Curley
  responded that the City has not received any legal action to date.

  Mayor Ury noted that CUSD Board of Trustees majority was awarded a "Radish" award
  by the Orange County Taxpayer's Association for their decision to take legal action against
  Mayor Ury and Mayor Tony Beal of the City of Rancho Santa Margarita.

14.  Economic Development Committee

  Council Members Sachs and Raths presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

15.  Proposition 64; Commonly referenced as the Adult Use of Marijuana Act

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  The following expressed their strong opposition to Proposition 64: Marilyn MacDougall,
  Executive Director of Drug Abuse is Life Abuse, M.V. and Rhonda Reardon, M.V.

  Council Member Sachs asked that the League's FAQ's and the Lozano Smith's companion
  document be posted on the City's website so the public can have access to that information.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Ury, direct staff to prepare
  an ordinance to ensure that Citywide prohibition of both medical and adult use (non-
  medical) marijuana sale, cultivation, etc. to be effective prior to November 8, 2016.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  5  September 13, 2016
   AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

*Item 18 was taken out of order.

18.  Consideration of a Resolution of the City Council of the City of Mission Viejo,
  California, Opposing the Adult Use of Marijuana Initiative — Commercial Sales of
  Non-Medical Marijuana Ballot Measure

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to
  adopt Resolution 16-46 Opposing the Adult Use of Marijuana Initiative - Commercial
  Sales of Non-Medical Marijuana Ballot Measure (Proposition 64).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

16.  Project V Local Circulator-Branding and Fare Structure

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Bob Breton, M.V.: expressed support for the local circulator shuttle and he stated that the
  success of this endeavor depends on the frequency of the trips, reliability, and publicity.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to (1) select the name
  MV Shuttle and the slogan “Connecting Mission Viejo”; (2) adopt OCTA’s bus fares as
  the base fare structure for the City’s Project V Local Transit Circulator and directed staff
  to determine what discounts will be offered in the following categories: Regular, Senior
  (60+) and Disabled, College Student, High School Student; (3) direct that there should be
  an initial no-fare period of 90 days to promote ridership of the new route; (4) direct staff to
  return in 90 days with feedback regarding the shuttle service at which time the Council will
  decide about fares and whether discounts shall be offered generally or only through
  coupons or passes to be obtained from certain locations and/or via the City's website; and
  (5) direct staff to ask OCTA to add Mission Viejo’s routes to its rider app and/or look at
  developing a stand-alone MV Shuttle app.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  6  September 13, 2016
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

17.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: referenced an email that he wrote to the City Council Members
  regarding the OCFA's unfunded liability on August 31, a copy of which he provided to the
  City Clerk for the public record.

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Raths

No comments.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs discussed a recent Orange County Register editorial article questioning
whether School Resource Officers are a benefit or a deterrent. He said the article appears to have
been structured after a Christian Science Monitor article which quoted a professor at Arizona State
University who stated that SRO's, in many cases, can be a negative influence because they take
advantage of any normal kid being a kid and escalating it up to an offense that goes on their
record. The Register article went on to say that SRO's have very little training and he noted that it
seems to be in vogue right now to slam police. Council Member Sachs expressed his aggravation
that one would assume that any police department would send an officer into a high school without
any training. He said that he has seen the Orange County Sheriff Department training outline which
confirms that the SRO's attend a 40-hour training class before they are ever assigned to a school
and they attend annual training thereafter. Council Member Sachs said that he recently had the
honor and privilege of playing in a golf tournament with a Mission Viejo SRO who is very engaged
with the students at the school where he works. The SRO told him that many parents stop him to
talk about the benefit that they and their kids have received from the SRO's presence at the
school. Council Member Sachs reminded his colleagues that at the last meeting, he talked about
how it is difficult to manage the language in a contract dealing with change orders. He said that
for contracts that necessitate an over-watch, it would be good to have a two-councilmember ad
hoc to oversee the contracts and he asked Mayor Ury to appoint Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum and
Council Member Raths to over-watch the Marguerite Aquatics Center project. He also asked staff
to watch the contingencies in bid contracts and to not overuse them. Council Member Sachs talked
about his comments six months ago when Santa Margarita Water District (SMWD) tore up the
beautiful streets in his neighborhood. At the time he was very upset but he asked for forgiveness
and said that SMWD has completed the task of adding recycled water to all of the landscaping and
replaced the plants in his neighborhood and it is gorgeous. Finally, he discussed the City's 9/11
anniversary service where he learned that at every fire station in Orange County, the firefighters
conduct a short remembrance of 9/11 at 9:03 a.m. each morning.

City Council Minutes  7  September 13, 2016
 Council Member Schlicht

19.  Support Congressman Darrell Issa’s Legislation for Local Control, Oversight and
  Licensing of Sober Living Homes

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report.

  Council Member Sachs said that he has spoken with Congressman Issa and there is no
  legislation at this point, it was just a comment that he made on the topic. The Council
  Members conveyed that they are not in favor of supporting this until the legislation has
  come forward and that they would like this added to the City’s legislative platform.

  Council Member Schlicht withdrew her recommendation for the time being.

Council Member Schlicht stated that in the Animal Shelter agenda item (#8,) a reader wouldn't
specifically find the dollar amount in the staff report. She said that the original budget was
$780,000 but with the contingencies, the new project amount is $963,182.75. It concerns
her especially because there is an $8 million Aquatics Center project coming up and she feels that
the City has trouble staying within budget. Council Member Schlicht asked the City Attorney
about the current curb painting project and the non-profit organization that is doing the
painting. She said the non-profit is possibly giving a token donation to children's organizations
and she expressed concern about ethical distribution of City funds. She also asked about the
CEQA process for the Aquatics Center pool rehab to which Assistant City Manager Rattay noted
that it was already done and there is no update required since there is no change in function at the
Aquatics Center. Council Member Schlicht announced that Patsy's Irish Pub will be hosting a
fundraiser where .75 cents of every pint of beer sold will go to the City's adopted military families
at Camp Pendleton. The dates are September 20, October 18, and November 22, 2016, from 6:00
to 9:00 p.m. She further announced that Caltrans is hosting an open house on the topic of managed
lanes. She noted that she is anti-toll road and fears that there will be implementation of toll lanes
in South Orange County without a vote of the public. In closing, she recognized the vicious attack
on our country 15 years ago on 9/11 with a quote from United Airlines Flight 93 passenger Todd
Beamer: "Let's Roll."

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum said that the 9/11 ceremony was great as was the program at the
Community Center on taking a stand against bullying. The latter was presented by PKSA Karate
Studio owner Bob Stewart. Mr. Stewart taught the participants practical ways to deal with bullying
and it was very beneficial for the kids. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum noted that a constituent has
expressed concern that Council Member Schlicht is being given preferential treatment on the
parking of her RV. She asked the City Attorney for the status of Council Member Schlicht’s RV
situation and noted that other homeowners in town pay for parking, while Council Member
Schlicht’s RV has been parked in her driveway for years. City Attorney Curley responded that at
this point there is a citation process underway and the City is looking at other mechanisms to
ensure enforcement. He said that the laws equally apply to everybody and although the City tries
City Council Minutes  8  September 13, 2016
 to give leeway for extenuating circumstances, things are moving forward in a very routine manner
through the legal process. Finally, Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum ended her comments with a video
of football players talking about their experience playing in the recent Honor Bowl games at
Mission Viejo High School.

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury noted that the City's 9/11 memorial event for Patriot Day was very nice and it has been
his goal to make sure that young people understand what this country went through. He recounted
a conversation earlier in the day with his 17 year-old son who had questions about what his dad’s
day was like on 9/11. Mayor Ury noted that his son was really asking probing questions and he
wanted to know about Todd Beamer and how the passengers on the plane were communicating
with the ground. He said that it was very nice to know that kids are learning about 9/11 in school
and it made him feel good to know that his son is engaged with the topic.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:13 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, September 27, 2016, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of September 27, 2016

City Council Minutes  9  September 13, 2016
